newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Antitrust gives icecream firms a licking.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Antitrust gives icecream firms a licking.

text.p: Italy's Antitrust authority slammed leading icecream makers in the country on Wednesday for freezing out competition.

After an investigation started last May, the body ruled that accords between the main firms in Italy - Unilever, Nestle, Sammantona and Sanson - imposing "freezer exclusivity" on retailers infringed anti-competition rules.
The Antitrust authority said in a statement that distribution contracts imposed by the big companies prevented icecream shops from being able to sell competitors' brands.
These contracts involved 162,000 sales points in Italy, equal to 68 percent of the total icecream retail network and accounting for 73 percent of overall sales in the sector.
The Antitrust authority said it gave the companies named 180 days to stop such anti-competition practices and to present written evidence they had done so.

It noted Italy was the European leader in the sector of icecream "impulse buying", a market double in size that of Germany and triple Spain's, with production in 1995 of some 123,000 tonnes worth 2.2 trillion lire ($1.4 billion) in terms of consumer prices.

Unilever, with its makes Algida, Sorbetteria di Ranieri and Eldorado, and Nestle, with Motta and Antica Gelateria del Corso, together had 70 percent of total sales in volume terms, the Antitrust body added.
